thread.title: Pennsylvania Senate approves bill enhancing breast cancer screening coverage
thread.title_full: Pennsylvania Senate approves bill enhancing breast cancer screening coverage

author: Luzerne Times
title: Pennsylvania Senate approves bill enhancing breast cancer screening coverage
text:
Elisabeth J. Baker, Pennsylvania State Senator from 20th District | Facebook
Elisabeth J. Baker, Pennsylvania State Senator from 20th District | Facebook
With bipartisan support, the Pennsylvania Senate has approved legislation to enhance the state's no-cost breast cancer screening law. The bill aims to ensure that diagnostic imaging is fully covered, eliminating financial barriers for patients. Senator Lisa Baker (R-20) backed the measure.
Senate Bill 88 builds on Act 1 of 2023, which provided no-cost preventive screenings for high-risk individuals. This new legislation guarantees that patients with abnormal results from supplemental screenings, such as MRIs or ultrasounds covered under Act 1, can access necessary follow-up diagnostic imaging at no cost. It also expands eligibility to include those at average risk, aligning state law with federal recommendations.
"As someone with dense breast tissue, I know firsthand how critical it is to have access to additional diagnostic imaging. Too often, the cost of that follow-up work stands between women and the answers they need," Baker said. "Senate Bill 88 removes that financial barrier and ensures patients can get timely, potentially lifesaving care. This is a compassionate and commonsense step forward, and I'm proud to support it."
While 26 other states offer no-cost supplemental breast screening since Act 1's passage, Pennsylvania remains unique in lacking guaranteed coverage for diagnostic imaging. Senate Bill 88 addresses this gap by allowing patients access to comprehensive care without financial burden.
The bill has garnered support from advocacy groups like the Pennsylvania Breast Cancer Coalition and the American Cancer Society and faces no opposition from insurers.
Senate Bill 88 now advances to the House of Representatives for further consideration.
